title: The Ink Smudge Story
markdown:
The student newspaper office hummed, a comforting sound to Nico the jackdaw, who loved things to be just so. Outside, night was gobbling the last of twilight. He straightened his chest feathers, trying to look very smart. Tonight he wanted a room full of important words. He had stacked paper neatly. Desk lamps cast a warm glow he hoped would chase away messy thoughts.

The most noticeable thing in the room was a smudge. Not just any smudge: a terrible, impossible-to-miss ink-blot sitting in the middle of the main story, which concerned the university’s new plan for helping the planet. Utterly avoidable, Nico felt, with a shiver.

“It’s just… so out of place.” He tilted his head, as if a different angle might erase it. His beak twitched. “So different from the careful words about the composting system. Like a stray punctuation mark went on a wild adventure.”

Across the room, Ada the cat stretched on a worn armchair, tabby fur rippling. She yawned, a silent pink cavern of tiny sharp teeth.

“Adventure, Nico? Or just a normal day?” Her voice was a low purr. Deadlines did not wait.

Nico wrung his claws. “But Ada, this is the Sentinel. We need to be clear. Honest. This is a stain on everything.” He flapped a wing toward the blot. “Louder than any perfect sentence. It mocks the interviews. It makes those long chats about commas seem silly.”

Ada stopped licking a paw. Amber eyes looked past him, as if considering a nap.

“Well, it is very black. It makes the white paper stand out, doesn’t it?”

Nico sighed, dry leaves skittering. He thought of his tidy office: staplers lined up, pens sorted by colour, the quiet smell of old paper and faint coffee. He had worked to make it a place for deep thought. All anyone would see was the blot.

“We are not in trouble,” he announced, trying for calm. He adjusted imaginary spectacles. “We are just… seen.”

Ada stopped grooming and looked right at him, gaze steady and kind.

“Nico. You’ve spent all evening making this room look like a perfect book. But it’s a student newspaper office on deadline night. It should look like things are happening. Work being done, even if it’s a little messy.” She flicked an ear, a sparkle in her eyes. “Besides, that smudge is the most interesting thing on that page. Makes you wonder how it happened. A runaway pen? A moment of overwhelm? A fight with an ink bottle?”

As she spoke, Nico looked out the grimy window. The sky was no longer twilight. It was a deep dark blue, spilled blueberry juice across the glass. Wonder pulled him from the smudge, the deadlines, the worry. He had been so focused on looking perfect he had almost missed the effort that went into the page, blot and all.

He looked back at the article, then at Ada. She gave him a tiny nod.

“Right.” He picked up a fresh pen. Not to erase: to draw. A neat small circle around the smudge. Beside it, in his clearest handwriting: Correction noted. More edits to come after thinking deeply about ink.

Ada let out a soft chuckle that filled the room.

“Now that’s writing. Gets right to the point, with a touch of smartness.”

The office did not go quiet. The feeling changed: not the tense hush of something about to go wrong, but the focused energy of a problem being solved. The blot was simply a mark on a page. Nico looked at his circle, then at the dark blue sky. The lamp caught the ink in a small honest glint. The stack of paper waited. Ada curled again, purring, while the Sentinel, smudge and all, faced the night.
